title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
summary: A triplet consists of three integers.
statement: A triplet consists of three integers. Given a 2D integer array of triplets and a target triplet, determine if the target can be formed by repeatedly applying an operation that merges two triplets into one with the maximum values of corresponding elements. Return true if the target can be achieved, otherwise return false.
constraints: There are 1 through 100000 triplets of positive values at most 1000.
target also has exactly three positive values.
A merge takes the coordinate-wise maximum; determine whether some sequence of merges can equal target.
hints: A triplet exceeding target in any coordinate can never participate because maxima cannot decrease.
Merge only component-wise safe triplets into an accumulated coordinate-wise maximum.
Succeed exactly when all three accumulated coordinates reach target.
Filtering is necessary by monotonicity of maximum, and every safe contributor may be merged without overshooting, so reaching all coordinates is sufficient.
editorial: Filtering is necessary by monotonicity of maximum, and every safe contributor may be merged without overshooting, so reaching all coordinates is sufficient.

tests.explanation: The first and third triplets merge to the target; the second must be excluded because its middle value is too large.
Every useful-looking triplet exceeds the target in at least one coordinate, so the target is impossible.
